propositions: A segmenting Markdown-to-wiki renderer must classify body segments into protected units (fenced code, HTML, regex-heavy blocks, ASCII tables), safe units (headings, quotes, lists, prose), and {noformat} blocks, rendering only safe units through pypandoc while preserving others byte-identically.
Prose arrow sequences (->/<-/<->/=>) must convert to Unicode forms before pandoc rendering, except within fenced code and backtick-delimited inline-code spans which remain byte-identical.

The pypandoc-binary==1.17 dependency must be optional under jira-dc extra, lazily imported with guard_import, and missing pypandoc or conversion failure must return exact input with one-per-process fallback warning.

ASCII tables detected as two or more pipe-bearing lines with delimiter row of pipes/colons/hyphens/whitespace must wrap exactly once in {noformat}, and existing {noformat} blocks must never nest through repeated rendering.
A corpus of 179 code-arrow and 70 table-erosion fixtures must demonstrate 68% body and 78% character enrichment with zero corruption of declared protected excerpts across five renderer passes.
Real pandoc with Jira writer availability must be a non-skipping test gate; all existing WikiTextCodec truncation, identity, and codec-law contracts must remain unchanged and green.
